name: G16 2024 (GU605) - quiet at the desk, strong in games
description: Measured on a GU605MY (Core Ultra 9 185H + RTX 4090 Laptop) in Ultimate GPU mode. Fans stay at their floor until the CPU is genuinely hot, ramp to full under sustained load, and the CPU runs a lower sustained power limit that keeps it OFF its 96C throttle point. Turbo is the plugged-in mode; Silent is used when the screen is off.

explain.performance_1: Plugged in: Turbo (1). The firmware preset with the highest limits; the curves below make it quiet anyway.
explain.performance_0: On battery: Balanced (0) instead of Turbo.
explain.auto_apply_1: Actually apply the Turbo fan curve (G-Helper saves curves but ignores them unless this is on).
explain.fan_profile_cpu_1: 0% until 70C (the fan sits at its ~2000 rpm floor), 20% at 74C, 100% at 96C. Flat enough that short bursts don't ramp.
explain.fan_profile_gpu_1: 0% until 60C so the GPU fan is OFF at the desk, 25% at 64C, 100% at 90C.
explain.auto_apply_2: Apply the Silent curve too (used when the screen is off).
explain.fan_profile_cpu_2: Silent CPU: same shape, gentler, capped at 60%.
explain.fan_profile_gpu_2: Silent GPU: off until 60C, capped at 60%.
explain.auto_boost_1: Windows CPU boost: Enabled (1). 'Efficient' modes let clocks sag in CPU-bound games.
explain.auto_apply_power_1: Actually apply the power limits below in Turbo.
explain.limit_slow_1: PL1 (sustained) 65 W instead of G-Helper's 80 W fix. Counter-intuitive but measured: at 80 W this chip pins at 96C and throttles to ~2.1 GHz; at 65 W it holds ~2.7 GHz. Battlefield 6 went from 67 to 80-100 fps CPU-side.
explain.limit_fast_1: PL2 (burst) 110 W. Short spikes keep their headroom.
explain.gpu_temp_1: GPU temperature target 75C instead of 87C. In CPU-bound games the GPU has headroom to spare, and a cooler GPU takes heat off the shared heatsink. Set back to 87 for GPU-bound games.

notes: Any non-zero point in a fan curve spins that fan at its minimum (~2000 rpm). Only a true 0 stops it.
The CPU fan will not stop while the CPU is warm no matter what the curve says; in Ultimate GPU mode the CPU idles at 64-75C, so expect ~2000 rpm at the desk.
G-Helper re-applies this profile on every screen-on and at startup, and logs it in %APPDATA%\GHelper\log.txt.
After a thermal repaste, re-test PL1 at 80 W: a cooler heatsink may let it run there without throttling.
